policy.negative_fixture_rule: retired modes, retired adapters, alternate acceptance paths, retired-source lanes, and removed feature-toggle behavior must be represented as strict rejection metadata
policy.validation_boundary: fixture metadata only; runtime acceptance scripts and public command-surface metadata are owned by other lanes
policy.legacy_positive_residue_policy: compatibility-looking positives are deleted or converted to tests/native rejection and strict-error fixtures
policy.runtime_dispatch_symbol_rule: runtime_dispatch_symbol is only present when execution.requires_live_runtime_dispatch is true
policy.large_surface_split_rule: large or legacy-looking fixture directories must be split by behavior owner before a fixture path can be cited as positive coverage

families.hard_cutover_rule: non-canonical grammar spellings are rejected; no parser compatibility mode positives
semantic positives prove canonical type/effect behavior; unsupported aliases and retired suffixes stay negative

families.metadata: IR expectation files paired with accepted source fixtures
families.hard_cutover_rule: IR expectations use canonical lowering only and must not encode alternate shim paths

families.metadata: checked-in manifest and artifact truth fixtures
families.hard_cutover_rule: manifest fixtures describe canonical JSON contracts and may not accept compatibility-era optional fields as success criteria

families.metadata: exit-code files for positives and meta.json failure contracts for negatives
families.hard_cutover_rule: runtime-like positives cannot stand in for runtime acceptance; unresolved dispatch, missing runtime symbols, and strict runtime diagnostics stay negative

families.metadata: compile-stage sidecars for source surfaces that are parsed but not runnable in the native hard-cutover surface
families.hard_cutover_rule: throws and ARC ownership qualifier runnable claims are explicit O3S221 rejections, not source-only shims or fallback execution paths

families.metadata: positive fixtures renamed away from compatibility-era wording while preserving canonical behavior
families.hard_cutover_rule: compatibility-looking positive names are replaced by canonical behavior names or moved to negative strict-error coverage

families.metadata: fixture data for command/library parity and comparison baselines
families.hard_cutover_rule: baseline comparison is provenance-only evidence, not interoperability, drop-in compatibility, fallback acceptance, or an alternate success path

owner_splits.split_rule: Accepted recovery fixtures are provenance for the phase that owns the behavior they exercise; this directory is not a generic positive support bucket.

owners.disposition: canonical syntax and selector-shape acceptance only
canonical type, bool-flow, and return-path semantics only
canonical lowering or ABI handoff evidence only; no runtime fallback acceptance
runtime-dispatch requirement evidence only when live dispatch remains canonical

owner_splits.split_rule: Executable positives are owned by e2e; phase-specific names inside this tree are witnesses for canonical behavior, not alternate phase support lanes.

owners.disposition: deterministic compile-link-run success through canonical Objective-C 3.0 behavior only
phase provenance for lowering contracts; the positive claim remains e2e-owned
live dispatch positives must name objc3_runtime_dispatch_i32 and require live runtime dispatch

owner_splits.split_rule: Negative execution fixtures are split by first failing owner and retired-surface disposition, not by path convenience.

owners.disposition: typed semantic, unsupported-feature, and conservative analysis rejection metadata
strict link-error evidence for required runtime symbols; not a fallback path
retired or unsupported surfaces are non-positive canonical rejection or strict-error contracts

owner_splits.split_rule: Root-level fixture names that look positive are provenance only until a canonical manifest entry assigns parser, sema, lowering, runtime, e2e, or canonical-rejection ownership.

owners.disposition: source and semantic model evidence only
lowering, IR, or artifact-shape evidence only
runtime-backed behavior evidence only after canonical runtime ownership is indexed
end-to-end release or packaging witnesses only
canonical rejection or strict-error evidence; never legacy-positive support
